title: Bound on an orthogonal Fourier component
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For any nonnegative integer $n$, function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and point $x\in\Omega^n$, the absolute value of the sum of the product Fourier terms whose indices differ from $0$ exactly on $S$ is at most $2^{|S|}\max_{y\in\Omega^n}|f(y)|$.
hypotheses_covered: probability measure on the sample space
